title: Prefill attention with HiFloat8 Q and K
formula: out = softmax(Q @ K^T / sqrt(128)) @ V per batch, HiFloat8 Q[B*MQ,128] and K[B*N,128] in uint8 carriers, BF16 V[B*N,128] and out[B*MQ,128], FP32 online state and accumulator
study_for: The minimal-edit precision experiment: only Q and K become HiFloat8 for the score matmul, while P, V, the online softmax VF and the PV matmul all stay at the BF16 baseline. The kernel says so in as many words at its entry, which makes this the right unit to read when asking what one quantisation step alone costs.
Read it beside `attention.a5_pfa_qk_fp8`, which is the same edit with E4M3 instead of HiFloat8, and beside `attention.a5_pfa_bf16`, which is the shared baseline both are measured against.

How a dtype torch cannot hold crosses the boundary: the kernel argument is `GM[u8, ...]` and `q.reinterpret(DT.hif8)` relabels the same bytes for the matmul, with the L1 tensors declared `DT.hif8` directly. The reference decodes those bytes through a value table built from exponent/fraction classes rather than through the execution codec, so a codec defect cannot be agreed to by both sides.

Stream-K sharding over the flat (m_tile, k_tile) grid rather than over M tiles alone: grep `fd_accum`, `fd_max`, `fd_sum`. A core boundary that lands inside an M tile makes that tile write an unnormalised partial state to the GM workspace, and after a vec-wide barrier `fd_merge_vf` rescales the two partials onto a common row max. `fd_matched` and `fd_split` are the same shape either side of that boundary.
do_not_copy_when: You want the all-HiFloat8 route. P and V here are BF16 on purpose; the units under `a5_pfa_hif8*` are the ones that carry HiFloat8 through the PV matmul as well.

More than two cores can own one query tile. The merge reads exactly two workspace slots per split tile, so a `block_dim` that cuts one M tile three ways, or that puts two interior boundaries in the same tile, merges the wrong pair without complaining. Each case here names a block_dim that satisfies the precondition; it is not a free knob.
Your head dimension is not 128. D=128 is wired into the tiling as TILE_M/TILE_N=128 and two 64-lane FP32 register chunks per output row, and is not a parameter despite being a kernel argument.
